1. Outside view. The Economist/YouGov tracker of Trump's approval has recently been fluctuating with a significant amount of noise between 33% and 39%, reflecting an average of 36.0% over the last ten available releases. The tracker frequently exhibits mean reversion, where a low release (such as 33% or 34%) is often followed by a jump back up toward the 36-38% range. A naive extrapolation would predict a bounce back from the recent low of 33.0% towards the historical mean, likely arriving around 35.5% to 36.0%.

2. Inside view. The events provided leading up to August 23, 2026, include President Trump pausing a border wall project in Texas due to local and environmental concerns and ordering the DoD to reduce military exercises with South Korea. Neither of these moves constitutes a major shock that would fundamentally alter the baseline of his public support. Pausing the wall project might marginally depress base enthusiasm, but reducing foreign military deployments often aligns with his "America First" messaging. Consequently, the polling will likely be driven more by statistical noise and typical mean-reverting panel dynamics than by any substantial swing in true public opinion. I expect a standard reversion to the ~35.5% mark.

3. Pre-mortem. If my forecast turns out badly wrong, it is likely because the 33.0% value was the beginning of a genuine downward trend rather than a noisy outlier, perhaps due to cumulative fatigue or an unmentioned ongoing scandal not fully captured in the daily event summaries. Alternatively, a delayed bounce-back could result in another low reading (e.g., 33-34%). To correct for this, I will keep the mean estimate slightly below the long-term average (at 35.5 rather than 36.0) and use a comfortably wide standard deviation.

4. Calibrate. Over the last 10 periods, the standard deviation of the raw values is ~2.05, and the week-to-week changes average about 3 points in magnitude. Given this high level of volatility, a standard deviation of 2.1 will ensure that a roughly 68% confidence interval captures any value between 33.4% and 37.6%, encompassing the bulk of the series' recent distribution.
